H&P – Detailed Clinical Note

Consult Summary:
19-year-old female with 1-week history of dysuria, urinary frequency, and pink-tinged urine; clinical picture consistent with acute uncomplicated cystitis.

History:
• Presenting complaint: Burning/stinging pain during urination and markedly increased urinary frequency.  
• Onset/progression: Began just under one week ago; symptoms persistent, limiting university attendance.  
• Character: Dysuria; dull aching suprapubic pain, worse during micturition; denies radiation to back/flanks.  
• Urine appearance: Pink discoloration noted today; no frank visible clots described.  
• Associated symptoms: No fever, chills, nausea, vomiting, loin pain, or new bowel changes.  
• Pertinent negatives: No vaginal discharge, no new GI symptoms beyond baseline IBS, no systemic symptoms.  
• Sexual/OB history: Sexually active with long-term boyfriend; combined OCP; last unprotected intercourse ≈1 week ago; LMP 2 weeks ago; uncertain pregnancy risk discussed.  
• Exposures: Tried cannabis once 1½ weeks ago (clinician advised cessation).

Past Medical History:
• Irritable Bowel Syndrome – variable stool consistency; takes antispasmodic for cramps.  
• No other chronic illnesses reported.

Medications:
• Combined oral contraceptive pill – dose/route/frequency not documented.  
• Mebeverine (probable) for IBS – dose/route/frequency not documented.  
Allergies:
• Clindamycin – adverse reaction (nature not detailed).

Social History:
• First-year university student (English); lives in student halls with flatmate.  
• Occasional social alcohol; denies regular tobacco; single trial of cannabis.  
• Supportive family living outside London.

Family History:
• No known bladder, kidney, or other notable hereditary conditions.

Physical Examination:
Not recorded (video consult; no in-person exam/vitals).

Investigations:
• Mid-stream urine (MSU) sample arranged for dipstick and culture/sensitivity.

Assessment & Plan:
Overall Impression:
Acute uncomplicated urinary tract infection (cystitis) most likely; low concern for pyelonephritis or other pathology at present.

DDx Integration (brief):
1. Acute cystitis/UTI – burning urination, frequency, mild suprapubic ache, pink urine; no systemic signs.  
2. Vaginal/urethral STI (e.g., chlamydia) – sexually active; however, no discharge, dyspareunia, or vaginal symptoms (opposing evidence).  
3. Hematuria from non-infective cause (e.g., stones) – pink urine; but absence of colicky flank pain (opposing).

Issue 1: Dysuria & urinary frequency  
• Assessment: Likely uncomplicated UTI (cystitis).  
• Plan:  
  – Empiric antibiotic: Trimethoprim or Nitrofurantoin 3-day course (exact agent per local guideline once MSU taken).  
  – Provide MSU for culture; adjust therapy if sensitivities dictate.  
  – Hydration advice: increase oral fluids.  
  – Analgesia: Paracetamol as needed.  
  – Safety-net: Seek urgent review for fever, flank/back pain, vomiting, or worsening symptoms.  
  – Follow-up: Reassess if no improvement within 1 week or sooner if concerns.

Issue 2: Contraception & pregnancy risk  
• Assessment: Uses combined OCP appropriately; last period 2 weeks ago; low but not zero pregnancy risk.  
• Plan:  
  – Advise to continue OCP regularly.  
  – Consider pregnancy test if menses delayed or symptoms persist/worsen.

Issue 3: Cannabis experiment & general health counseling  
• Assessment: Single recent use; patient motivated to avoid ongoing use.  
• Plan: Brief advice to abstain from cannabis; reinforce safe alcohol limits; no further intervention required.

General plan items: None additional.

Quality checks:
• Missing vitals and physical exam elements – telemedicine context noted.  
• Medication doses/frequencies not documented.  
• No explicit documentation of OTC drug use besides advised paracetamol.  
• Transcript audio satisfactory; no contradictions between transcript and DDx.
